    Both managers left more than 47 points on the bench. Quinn won anyway, and John has nobody to blame but himself.

Patrick hangs 204.88 and takes the top spot

Two weeks ago Patrick's team posted 71.36, the lowest score of the season. On Sunday the same roster put up 204.88, the highest score of the season, and beat Tuck Dynasty by 67.2, the biggest blowout of the year. Dobbin on ur Rob till im Worthy sits atop both the standings and the power rankings at 3-1.

Tetairoa McMillan did most of the damage with 14 catches for 192 yards, two touchdowns and 47.2 points, the best individual week anyone has posted this season. Nico Collins added 32.8 and Bijan Robinson 31.7, so Patrick could shrug off David Montgomery's 4.3.

Elsewhere, managers had a rough time choosing starters. The league left 280.46 points on benches, and in three of the five games the loser had enough on the pine to win. Tucker scored the third-most points in the league and still fell to 0-4.

McMillan goes for 47.2 as Patrick buries Tucker by 67.2

Dobbin on ur Rob till im WorthyPatrick · 204.88
by 67.20
TUCK
Tuck DynastyTucker · 137.68

Dobbin on ur Rob till im Worthy beat Tuck Dynasty 204.88 to 137.68, a 67.2-point margin that is the largest of the season. Patrick beat his 138.5 projection by more than 66 points.

Tetairoa McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two scores for 47.2 points. Nico Collins had 32.8 and Bijan Robinson ran for 145 yards and two touchdowns for 31.7. David Montgomery's 4.3 on 10 carries was the only real dent.

Tucker did his part. Kyren Williams scored 36.7, Sam LaPorta 22.4 and Jake Bates went 4-for-4 on field goals for 18.4, and 137.68 would have beaten every other team on the slate. Emeka Egbuka's 3.3 didn't help, but nothing short of a miracle was beating 204.88.

Tucker scored 137.68 and lost by 67.2. Some weeks the schedule is the opponent.

Margin 22.50 · Bench cost the game

Doubs scores 23.8 on Thomas's bench while Rice posts a zero

China's Greatest FearNani · 142.02
by 22.50
She Burrowed her fingers in PepThomas · 119.52

China's Greatest Fear beat She Burrowed her fingers in Pep 142.02 to 119.52, a 22.5-point margin. CeeDee Lamb caught 17 passes for 189 yards and a score for 43.3 points, and Javonte Williams found the end zone three times for 31.3.

Thomas lost this one in his own lineup. Rashee Rice started and scored zero against a 15.3 projection, while Romeo Doubs sat on the bench with 23.8 and two touchdowns. Thomas's bench held 39.9 points, comfortably enough to cover the 22.5-point gap.

That wasted a good day from the starters who did show up. Puka Nacua had 29.7, Chuba Hubbard ran for 122 yards and two scores for 27.9, and Joe Burrow threw for 428 yards for 26.72. Nani even won with the Chiefs D/ST scoring 1.

A zero in the lineup, 23.8 on the bench, and a 22.5-point loss. The math is not complicated.

Waddle on ma Johnson beat Njigba Please 121.52 to 107.28, a 14.24-point margin. Kenneth Walker III carried the load with 22 carries for 177 yards and two touchdowns for 32.9 points.

Luke didn't make it easy on himself. Jared Goff threw for 412 yards and 23.48 on the bench while Josh Allen started and scored 18.52. Garrett Wilson managed 5.7 on three catches, and Jahmyr Gibbs scored 17.7 against a 27.3 projection.

Christian's offense didn't show up. His top scorer was kicker Will Reichard, who went 5-for-5 on field goals for 20, and TreVeyon Henderson managed 4.2. Njigba Please was projected for 127 and scored 107.28, which ended their run at the top.

When your kicker is your leading scorer, your offense has some explaining to do.

Margin 11.84 · Bench cost the game

Chase vanishes and Daniel's bench costs him again

CBBC
Chase Brown the Ball CarrierCarson · 109.00
by 11.84
Little young black childrenDaniel · 97.16

Chase Brown the Ball Carrier beat Little young black children 109 to 97.16, an 11.84-point margin that was the closest game of the week. Daniel's bench had 29.8 points on it, more than enough to win.

The lineup was the problem. Kenyon Sadiq started at tight end and caught nothing for zero points, while Devaughn Vele, who Daniel dropped and then claimed back this week, scored 17.4 on the bench. Ja'Marr Chase managed 5.7 against a 21.2 projection, and Parker Washington added 2.

Carson won without playing well. He scored 109, the seventh-best total of the week, and benched Alvin Kamara's 22.8 while DJ Moore started and put up 2.7. Chase Brown had 19.1 on 11 catches and George Kittle added 19, which was just enough.

Seventh-best score, a 3-1 record. Carson is winning the schedule lottery.

Nabers sits on John's bench as Quinn survives his own Monangai blunder

Rushing to RetirementQuinn · 109.14
by 15.22
malik nJohn · 93.92

Rushing to Retirement beat malik n 109.14 to 93.92, a 15.22-point margin, and 93.92 was the lowest score in the league this week. John's bench held 47.6 points, which would have won the game easily.

Malik Nabers had 112 yards, a touchdown and 25.2 points on John's bench. In the starting lineup, Saquon Barkley got two carries for 2 points and Dalton Kincaid caught one ball for 1.7. Tee Higgins had 28.7 and Jonathan Taylor 22.7, but nobody else did much.

Quinn got lucky on his own mistakes. Kyle Monangai carried 30 times for 146 yards and two scores for 30 points on the bench, while Davante Adams started and scored 7.2. Quinn left 51.62 points on the bench, the most of anyone this week, and still won behind Chris Olave's 21.6.

Quinn left 51.62 on the bench and won anyway. John only left 47.6, and that was enough to lose.

Draft watch

Patrick took Tetairoa McMillan in the fifth round, 42nd overall, and got the season's best single week out of him with 47.2. Thomas found the late-round steal in Chuba Hubbard, an eighth-rounder taken 76th overall who scored 27.9. He also had the early-round bust: Rashee Rice, a third-round pick at 25th overall, started and scored zero. CeeDee Lamb (11th overall, 43.3), Kenneth Walker III (20th, 32.9) and Nico Collins (19th, 32.8) all paid off as early picks.
